dataset_fields.title: Texas Water Well Reports (TDLR Submitted Driller's Reports)
dataset_fields.notes:
The Submitted Driller's Reports Database contains water well reports submitted to the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR) from February 2001 to present (~680,000 statewide point records). Each record locates a reported well and carries attributes such as well type, proposed use, county, owner, completion date, and borehole depth.

Published by the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) as a public ArcGIS FeatureServer and linked here as an external reference for the SUBSIDE catalog. It is also registered as the `well-reports` map overlay in the `subside-context` STAC collection (loaded viewport-by-viewport from the FeatureServer). Documentation: https://www.twdb.texas.gov/groundwater/data/drillersdb.asp

extras.collection_method_description: Water well reports submitted to TDLR by licensed drillers as a regulatory requirement.
extras.quality_assurance_description: Records reflect driller-submitted reports as received by TDLR; locations are not field-verified.
extras.caveats_usage: Well locations are derived from submitted driller's reports and may be approximate; records reflect reports as submitted to TDLR and have not been field-verified. Coverage begins February 2001, so wells completed earlier are generally not represented.
extras.attribution: Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) / Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR)

fields.description: Point layer of submitted water well reports (TDLR Submitted Driller's Reports, Feb 2001-present; ~680,000 features, EPSG:4326). Query via the ArcGIS REST API (f=geojson / f=json / PBF); maxRecordCount is 2,000, so consumers should page or query by bounding-box envelope.
Service root for the TWDB WellReports FeatureServer (service metadata, layer list, and capabilities).
TWDB documentation page describing the Submitted Driller's Reports Database, its contents, and access options.

dataset_fields.title: NGS Datasheets — Stable GNSS Control Marks
dataset_fields.notes:
Geodetic control marks from the NOAA National Geodetic Survey (NGS) Integrated Database, published as datasheets. This reference filters the ~1,000,000 datasheets to the marks the SUBSIDE velocity workflow cares about: those that are GNSS/GPS-usable (SAT_USE = 'Y') and physically stable (STABILITY class A or B — marks expected to hold their position/elevation well), ~72,000 statewide/nationwide point records.

Why SUBSIDE references them: the velocity workflow fits a linear rate to OPERA DISP-S1 InSAR displacement, which is a *relative* measurement. Stable, satellite-suitable NGS marks (CORS, PACS/SACS, and high-stability monuments) provide absolute reference / validation control to tie or sanity-check those relative velocities. Each mark carries its PID, name, stability and satellite-use codes, datum/epoch, ellipsoidal and orthometric heights, and a link back to its full NGS datasheet.

Published by NOAA/NGS as a public ArcGIS FeatureServer and linked here as an external reference for the SUBSIDE catalog. It is also registered as the `ngs-gnss-stable` map overlay in the `subside-context` STAC collection (loaded viewport-by-viewport, server-side filtered to SAT_USE='Y' AND STABILITY IN ('A','B')). NGS datasheet field reference: https://geodesy.noaa.gov/DATASHEET/dsdata.pdf

extras.collection_method_description: Geodetic control marks observed and adjusted by NOAA/NGS and cooperating agencies; positions and heights are published as NGS datasheets in the NGS Integrated Database.
extras.quality_assurance_description: Positions are published by NGS with accuracy and order/class codes; this reference is further filtered to stable (STABILITY A/B), satellite-usable (SAT_USE='Y') marks suitable as velocity reference control.
extras.caveats_usage: Filtered to GNSS-usable, stability-class A/B marks; stability classes are NGS monument-stability judgments, not subsidence measurements, and last-recovery condition varies by mark. The relative quality codes describe each mark's published accuracy at its epoch and should be reviewed before using a mark as absolute control.

fields.description: Point layer of NGS datasheet control marks (ALL_DATASHEETS; geometry EPSG-geographic NAD83(2011), query with outSR=4326). ~1M total marks; SUBSIDE consumes the SAT_USE='Y' AND STABILITY IN ('A','B') subset (~72k). maxRecordCount is 2,000, so consumers should page or query by bounding-box envelope (f=geojson supported).
Service root for the NGS Datasheets FeatureServer (service metadata, layer list, and capabilities).
NOAA/NGS documentation describing the datasheet format and every field (PID, STABILITY, SAT_USE, datum/epoch, accuracy codes, etc.).
NGS datasheet portal: documentation and tools to retrieve datasheets by PID, location, or survey.
